Prep+Eat · v1.1 · sharing

The recipe share page

What a person who does not have Prep+Eat sees when someone sends them a recipe. Four states, plus the thing most of them will actually see first: the preview card in a chat.

This is Claude's design, not Thomas's. No Figma frame exists for this page, so every choice below is an improvisation made to give you something concrete to react to. The colour, type, spacing and radii are real Sebell DS tokens; the composition and all the copy are mine.

Everything I invented rather than derived is listed at the bottom, under What I made up. The two worth arguing about first are the sender's name and the fact strip.

First, the part that does the work

Nearly everyone meets this feature as a link in a chat, and decides in about a second whether to tap. The unfurl card is not packaging for the page – for a mouth-to-mouth feature it is the product, which is why it needs server-rendered tags rather than a page that fills itself in afterwards.

The page itself

Light-only, matching the app – dark was deferred for v1, so showing this page in dark would misrepresent it. Drawn at 320pt because essentially every open is on a phone.

What I made up

Everything here is a judgement call with no frame behind it. Listed so you can overrule them individually rather than reacting to the page as a whole.

The sender's first name, twice
✅ Approved by Thomas, 2026-08-17. "Pia shared a recipe with you", and again in the wall. This is the single biggest thing on the page and it is the reason the teaser can work at all: the ask comes from a person the reader knows, not from us. A wall that says "Get the app to see this" is a paywall; one that says "Pia's recipe is waiting for you" is a message from Pia.
It needs a spec change. The snapshot in recipe_shares does not currently carry the sharer's first name. It should. And it is a genuine privacy decision, not just a field: it puts a real person's name on a public URL that anyone holding the link can load.
✅ Description + the three time labels – Thomas, 2026-08-17
Replaces a fact strip I had proposed ("12 ingredients · 7 steps"), which he did not want. The page carries the recipe's own short description and the same Total / Prep / Cook labels the recipe screen uses, so it reads as a piece of the app rather than a marketing page about it.
On YOUR OWN recipes only. An imported recipe's description is scraped verbatim from the source – JSON-LD, or the page's own meta description (recipe-import.ts:362) – so it is dropped along with the photo. The times survive either way: minutes are facts, and facts are not anybody's property.
✅ No page title on the generated-card version – Thomas, 2026-08-17
The card carries the title because it must stand alone in the chat preview, so the page no longer repeats it underneath and goes straight to the description. The duplicate flagged here before is resolved.
"Already have it? Open the recipe"
Not a nicety. Universal links silently fail inside in-app browsers – Facebook's and Instagram's especially – so a share sent through those lands on this page even for people who have the app. Without this line they are asked to install something they already own.
Revoked reads differently from not-found
A revoked share still has a row, so we know who shared it and can name her. A bad token has no row and must stay generic. Two states, two voices, because we genuinely know different things.
The green wall block
surface/primary/lightest behind the ask, to separate it from the recipe without a hard rule. It is the only coloured area on the page, so it is doing the work of "this is the bit that asks something of you".
What I deliberately left out
No ingredient list, no method, no App Store badge (a plain DS button instead – the real one is a fixed Apple asset and would be the only foreign object on the page), no cookie banner, and no navigation. The page has one job.
✅ SETTLED: we republish nothing of an imported recipe – Thomas, 2026-08-17
Briefly reopened and then closed: *"don't publish the text or the photo."* An imported recipe's photo AND its description both belong to the site it came from, so a share page carries neither. Only the title, the times, and the sender's name – a title is too short to protect, minutes are facts, and the name is ours to give.
This is why the teaser was chosen, and it holds: the page publishes almost nothing copyrightable, so the unanswered legal question stays off the critical path. The cost is the thin card above, which is a real conversion cost and worth watching once it ships.
🎉 And it needs NO new column. I had specced a photo_source field set at import. Unnecessary: recipes.source_url has existed since migration 0006 and already answers the question – set means imported, null means typed by hand. One item removed from the build.
Known edge, not worth solving yet: import a recipe and then replace the photo with your own, and source_url is still set, so your own photo is suppressed. Conservative in the safe direction. Per-field provenance would fix it if it ever matters.
